To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the biosynthetic pathway of endogenous neutral endopeptide in primary cultures of proximal tubule kidney cells is very similar to the pathway followed by the same protein when expressed in a heterologous epithelial cell system, the MDCK line.
primary cultures of kidney PCT cells represent an excellent system for studying the biogenesis and polarized targeting of microvillar proteins.
primary cultures of PTC cells represent a new system to investigate the biogenesis of endogenous proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biosynthetic pathways of proteins and their intracellular sorting in kidney cells.
the biosynthesis and intracellular transport of the membrane protein NEP in kidney proximal convolted tubule cells.
the biogenesis and targeting of endogenous proteins and the molecular basis of epithelial polarity in primary cell cultures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NEP is synthesized as a precursor protein and is transported through the secretory pathway to the apical membrane of PCT cells.
the NEP protein in the kidney PCT cells has the same molecular characteristics as in the intestine, but that the NEP mRNA is different.
the biosynthesis of endogenous NEP molecules is not altered by culture conditions, and that the polarized distribution of the enzyme is maintained in PCT cells grown in defined medium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NEP is synthesized in the rough endoplasmic reticulum, transported to the Golgi, and sorted in a polarized fashion into the apical plasma membranes.
NEP biosynthesis and apical sorting in PCT cells are similar to those in other epithelial cells.
the biosynthesis of endogenous proteins, such as NEP, is a complex process which is dependent on the presence of a specific microenvironment, and which is not necessarily identical for all proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PCT cells can be used as a functional model to study the molecular mechanisms involved in the biogenesis of microvillar proteins.
the biogenic pathway for NEP is similar in PCT cells and MDCK cells.
primary cultures of PTC cells represent a model system with which to investigate protein biogenesis and sorting in epithelial cells.
